title: Hundreds march in Brussels against antisemitism and support Israel

tea.why: Protesters marched to denounce organised antisemitism and show steadfast support for Israel.
tea.want: They demanded freedom, security, dignity, peace, and equal rights for all communities.
tea.changed: Nov 22: Hundreds marched through central Brussels from Central Station to the Palace of Justice.

summary: Hundreds of demonstrators marched through central Brussels to protest against antisemitism, call for coexistence, and express support for Israel. The rally was organised by the Belgian Alliance for Peace in the Middle East, an umbrella initiative that includes the European Jewish Association and the Forum of Jewish Organizations in Belgium. Participants gathered outside Brussels Central Station, walked past the Great Synagogue, and concluded their march at the Palace of Justice. The crowd included Jewish community members, non-Jewish allies, Christians for Israel, Antwerp Imam Nordine Taouil, and members of the Iranian diaspora carrying flags and portraits of Reza Pahlavi. US Ambassador Bill White and Israeli Ambassador David Saranga also joined the demonstration. Police heavily deployed along the route, and the march concluded without incidents or counterprotests.
organizers: Belgian Alliance for Peace in the Middle East
Forum of Jewish Organizations in Belgium
demands: Promote peace, dialogue, and equal rights for all communities in the Middle East
response: Police deployed heavily along the route, blocking off the roadway and stationing officers every 10 meters, according to news reports.

crowd.text: Organizers estimated turnout at roughly 1,000 participants, while Belgian media reported between 600 and 800 attendees.

updates.text: Hundreds of demonstrators marched through central Brussels against antisemitism, joined by US and Israeli ambassadors.
